sources.title: Agustín Azkarate: archaeology, linguistics and rock churches of Late Antiquity, 2018
sources.note: Printed61 abstract on permeable frontier and contested linguistic boundaries;62 discovery1987 and sixth/seventh-century cemeteries. No grave goods equated with a precise language or fixed ethnicity.

sources.title: Basque Cultural Heritage Centre: Arkeoikuska 1996, San Pelayo excavation
sources.note: Printed165 English abstract and170 Spanish report: sixth/seventh-century amber beads, wooden bowl metal fittings and globular pottery, with contextual distinctions. Indexed original full passages checked.

sources.title: University of the Basque Country: food in early medieval villages, 2023
sources.note: Fifth/ninth-century ten-site comparison, regional Basque plant/millet-rich diets, limitations of status inference. Regional sample not universal menu or ethnic diagnostic.

sources.title: University of the Basque Country: medieval watering and manuring evidence, 2022
sources.note: 50 charred-seed samples from Aistra/Zornoztegi fourth/fourteenth centuries. Low/moderate water, near-absent manure, possible legume rotation and contrasting settlement roles. Preserve long chronology and hypothesis status.

sources.title: Etxepare Basque Institute: Linguae Vasconum Primitiae
sources.note: 1545 Bordeaux,15 poems, Lower Navarrese Garazi dialect, heuscara/beçala historical spellings, surviving Paris copy. Do not repeat broad exclusively-oral simplification or conjectured book burnings.

sources.title: Etxepare Basque Institute: A Collection of Prints, introductory motto
sources.note: PDFindex4 trilingual introduction exact Euskara, jalgi hadi mundura and English translation. This is modern-spelling institutional quotation of Etxepare, explicitly not an original1545 facsimile transcription.

sources.title: Albaola: investigation of the San Juan wreck
sources.note: Research institution primary account: Selma Huxley archival clues, wreck discovery1978 in RedBay, construction research from original timbers.

sources.title: Etxepare Basque Institute: contemporary language and culture
sources.note: Current official public agency statement supports living culture and international creative/educational work; no claim of one unified historical Basque state.

sources.title: Sámi Parliament of Finland: people, languages and institutions
sources.note: Official FAQ: homeland across four countries, multiple Uralic languages, living people and representative institution. Imported1500BCE to 800dates are not evidence for ethnic formation or extinction.

sources.title: University of Helsinki: diverse livelihoods at Levänluhta
sources.note: Research account: IronAge isotope food patterns, sea/land/freshwater, continued seventh-century marine contribution; genetic and place-name connections with Sámi. Connections qualified, not DNA-as-ethnicity.

sources.title: Holmqvist and colleagues: metal objects from Levänluhta, 2019
sources.note: Original abstract/introduction indexed: water cemetery circa300 to 800, at least98 individuals, mostly women/children. No evidence for older famine/battle theories; avoid such guesses.

sources.title: Pelletier and colleagues: reindeer domestication and teeth, 2023
sources.note: Introduction: gradual and geographically variable herding development, early mixed economy, draught/decoy/milking roles. Do not claim all ancient Sámi were large-herd pastoralists.

sources.title: Hedman, Olsen and Vretemark: Hunters, herders and hearths, 2015
sources.note: Direct full primary paper. pp3 to 5 rows, tentative tent households and dates mainly late11th/late13th centuries; p6 iron fishhook/knife/hide scraper/comb/tinderflint; abstract bone species. Counts omit87% denominator ambiguity.

sources.title: Max Planck DOBES: Kola Sámi geography and siidas
sources.note: Siida section: historic seasonal movement and winter reunion; Soviet forced coastal relocation; social ties continue. Avoid unsupported assignment to800orallSámi.

sources.title: Sámi Museum Siida: permanent and open-air exhibitions
sources.note: Skolt Heritage House: authentic homestead plus reconstructed earlier buildings from literature/oral evidence, smoke sauna and root-sewn boat. Modern museum displays, not excavated IronAge structures.

sources.title: Sámi Museum Siida: Northern Ostrobothnia collection return, 2024
sources.note: January16,2024 primary notice; approximately400 objects,1797 Enontekiö cheese mould,1730 crossbow stocks, intergenerational craft learning.

sources.title: Sámi Parliament of Finland: language nests
sources.note: Direct full official description: early childhood immersion, adults use target language from start, children choose language; cultural revitalization.

sources.title: Sámi Museum Siida: exhibition renewal and its Inari Sámi title
sources.note: Direct page: exact Enâmeh láá mii párnááh and These lands are our children, explicitly title of Matti Morottaja poem in Inari Sámi. Modern title used for2022exhibition, not ancientwriting;6originalwords only.

sources.title: UiT Arctic University of Norway: Northern Sámi communication phrases
sources.note: Direct university NorthernSámi phrase list: Movt manná? / How are you? Modern orthography, not a reconstructed prehistoric sentence.
